title: DbGate
name: dbgate
description: Database manager in the browser for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite, MongoDB, Redis and more: browse and edit tables, write queries, compare schemas, draw diagrams and import or export data. Source: https://github.com/dbgate/dbgate

env.name: DBGATE_PASSWORD
env.label: Password (required)
env.description: For logging in as admin. DbGate has no login at all without one, hence required.

env.name: DBGATE_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Set a password before you deploy, since the stack won't start without one. Then open http://<your-host>:3600 (or whichever port you picked) and log in as admin. Each browser gets asked once about anonymous usage analytics, which stay off unless you say yes. Add your databases with New Connection, and use dockerhost as the server for one published on the Docker host itself. A restart logs you out, nothing else is lost. Saved connections, queries and uploads live in the dbgate-data volume. Whenever someone opens it, DbGate's server also asks dbgate.cloud for new shared scripts and a premium advert, mentioning which kinds of database you use. Docs: docs.dbgate.io
